To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is evidence of a growing use of contract labour by employers, but that the evidence is not conclusive.

there is evidence that the use of contract labour is growing, that this is linked to the growth of contingent labour in the economy as a whole, and that it reflects a new approach to human resource management.

there has been substantial growth in the use of labour contracting by major employers, but the evidence for a causal link between this and the development of more strategic human resource strategies is weak.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the changing nature of the labour market, and the extent to the extent to which this reflects a shift in the nature of the employment relationship.
the changing nature of employment in Britain in the 199os, and with the extent to which the labour market is becoming segmented.

the extent to which the labour force strategies of major employers are being reshaped in response to changing competitive conditions and, in particular, the extent to which they are being restructured in ways which reflect the increasing importance of business strategy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of contract workers is increasing in many industries and that this is part of a broader shift to more flexible staffing policies.

the growth of labour contracting is not simply the product of a labour market in which the demand for labour is weak, but that it is also the result of a growing trend towards the development of segmented labour force and human resource strategies, which are increasingly linked to business strategies.

, although there is no evidence of a general shift to the 'contingent workforce' or a 'contingent economy', the growth of contract labour is a significant and increasingly important feature of the labour market, with implications for the future structure of the employment relationship.

the evidence supports the view that the strategic use by employers of segmented and flexible labour force strategies has developed strongly in Britain in the 199os and will continue to do so.

there is no one best way to staff a firm and that the best staffing strategy is one that is customized to the needs and goals of a firm and its workforce.
